content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] [article_no] with [product_name] expansion modules. The CPU's display/button panel is completely unresponsive except for the backlight, so I've been using it effectively as a non-display unit. Although it's an older [product_name] with some issues, it's worked well until now. Recently, I made some updates to the program and added a few new sensors. After these changes, I ran tests and simulated a power outage while the unit was running. Now, the device does not automatically return to RUN mode when power is restored. Everything else, including the expansion modules, appears to be functioning normally, and pressing the RUN button in the programming software starts the device with no errors. I've repeated this process several times. I could try undoing my recent program changes, but since everything works fine when started manually, I'm hesitant. I've also attempted clearing data and re-downloading the program. As far as I know, there are no settings or blocks in this [version_no] to control RUN/STOP behavior; it's supposed to resume RUN mode if power was lost during RUN. Please let me know if this understanding is incorrect. Any advice would be appreciated!

The [product_name] should return to the mode it was in at the time of power failure. For example, if it was in RUN, it should resume RUN when power is restored; if it was in STOP, it should stay in STOP. This behavior is set by the firmware and cannot be changed. If your device is not behaving this way, there may be a defect.
Thank you for the clarification. This matches what I thought. I will likely replace the unit and keep the faulty one for testing or hobby use.

analysis.insight_summary: Users noticed that a [product_name] [version_no] and [article_no] does not resume RUN mode automatically after power restoration, contrary to the expected firmware behavior. All modules operate correctly with no errors when manually entered into RUN mode, but requiring manual intervention disrupts the expected seamless operation and casts doubt on the system’s reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] to automatically resume RUN mode after a power outage if it was previously running, without needing any manual actions.
